02 Traceability matrix

Bangla name: ট্রেসেবিলিটি ম্যাট্রিক্স

← Contents · Endpoint index · Reverse index

Every business feature, and the technical things it touches. Three tables:

  1. §2 Feature → service — which backend service implements each feature
  2. §3 Feature → endpoint — which HTTP endpoint each screen calls
  3. §4 Feature → state — which queue, Redis key, table and external system each feature touches

Use §2 and §3 when you have a screen and want to know where its behaviour lives. Use §4 and the reverse index when you have a table, queue or Redis key and want to know who writes it.

1. Conventions

Column Meaning
Service The backend service that owns the behaviour
Endpoint The primary external path; — means the feature makes no HTTP call
Queue The SQS queue it produces to or consumes from; — means none
Redis The keys it reads or writes; — means none
Store The table, bucket or external store it writes
Ext An external system it depends on

A feature may span several rows when it genuinely does. Where a cell says same as above, the two features share the same component.

4. Feature → state

4.1 Queue ownership

Every message, its producer and its consumer. There is no dead-letter handling in code for any of them, and the retry counter never advances (Q-09).

Queue Produced by Consumed by Features
OrderSuccess Booking (paid order) Ticketing TicketGenerationService P-06, S-07
EventCapacity Booking (seat change) Booking LevelCapacityUpdateService, EventLiveCapacityUpdateService S-01, S-02
VatChallanProcessing Booking (Paid callback) Scheduler VatChallanProcessingService S-10, P-06
TicketSigning Ticketing (PDF ready) Ticketing S-08
TicketProcessing Ticketing (reserved) Utility TicketProcessingService S-09, A-12
FirebaseNotification PushNotification Scheduler FirebaseNotificationService S-11, X-23

5. Gaps in the matrix

Gap What is missing Query
Identity API endpoints Not in the repository, so they appear in no service's route table Q-01
OneID endpoints Configured under [see User Secrets]; locally a dummy Q-06
Agent client The endpoint exists, the client does not Q-07
Notification templates The external service holds the text and channel choice Q-05
CloudFront token consumer Nothing in the backend reads signedToken Q-50
Table ownership Several tables are mapped ExcludeFromMigrations by more than one service, so "which service owns this table" is not always answerable Q-02
